evidence.experimental_conditions: case reports; concentration unspecified
evidence.support_text: Two case reports were reported with positive patch tests to t-butyl alcohol. This indicates a human sensitization outcome.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported); patch tests on 148 patients suspected of cosmetic contact dermatitis at Sakai Municipal Hospital from 1989 to 1992
evidence.support_text: Fujimoto et al. (1997) reported that from 1989 to 1992, 148 patients suspected of cosmetic contact dermatitis were tested with cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported) and 3 reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported); patch tests on 238 patients suspected of cosmetic contact dermatitis at Sakai Municipal Hospital over a 5-year period
evidence.support_text: Higashi et al. (1986) reported 21 reactions to cinnamyl alcohol in 238 patients suspected of cosmetic contact dermatitis at Sakai Municipal Hospital; dose and vehicle were not reported.

evidence.experimental_conditions: cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported); patients with occupational contact dermatitis; 1978-1995; 2793 patients suspected contact dermatitis, 442 diagnosed occupational
evidence.support_text: During 1978-1995, among 2793 patients with suspected contact dermatitis, 442 were diagnosed with occupational contact dermatitis; patch testing with cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported) elicited positive reactions in 15 of these occupational contact dermatitis patients.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol tested initially at 2% in petrolatum (1979–1983), then 1% in petrolatum (from 1984), with 5% sorbitan sesquioleate added as emulsifier from October 1991; Finn Chambers, Scanpor tape on upper back for 2 days; readings on days 2, 3, and 5–7.
evidence.support_text: In a study from 1979 to 1992, 8215 patients were patch tested with the fragrance mix; 367 of the 449 positive patients were further tested with individual constituents. Cinnamyl alcohol was tested at 2% in petrolatum initially then reduced to 1% with sorbitan sesquioleate added later. Positive reactions to cinnamyl alcohol were observed in 40 patients, with 24 additional questionable reactions (Johansen and Menne, 1995).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol, dose and vehicle not reported; epicutaneous tests as above.
evidence.support_text: In the same study, 156 patients with pure allergy to cosmetics (without irritation) showed 6 reactions to cinnamyl alcohol (Broeckx et al., 1987).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol, dose and vehicle not reported; epicutaneous tests with standard battery, cosmetic series, fragrance materials.
evidence.support_text: A study of cosmetic intolerance in 5202 patients using epicutaneous tests; 34 reactions to cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported) were observed in all patients (Broeckx et al., 1987).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol, dose and vehicle not reported; same method as above.
evidence.support_text: Additionally, reactions to cinnamyl alcohol were observed in 13 out of 130 patients with a cosmetic and iatrogenic dermatitis (Dooms-Goossens et al., 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cinnamyl alcohol, dose and vehicle not reported; Van den Bend chambers on Micropore tape; readings at 48 and 96 h according to ICDRG guidelines.
evidence.support_text: Dooms-Goossens et al. (1992) reported that among 462 patients reacting to cosmetics, 27 also reacted to cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported).

evidence.experimental_conditions: closed patch test; test substance: alcohol (as ingredient in shampoo)
evidence.support_text: A 56-year-old alcoholic man, subjected to disulfiram therapy, developed generalized pruritic macular rash after using a shampoo. A closed patch test later confirmed the reaction to alcohol, one of the ingredients in the shampoo.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Closed patch tests on 577 patients; 0.05–0.5% cinnamyl alcohol in base cream or 99% ethanol; patches applied to back, forearm, inside upper arm for 24–48 h; reactions read 30 min after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: Takenaka et al. (1986) conducted closed patch tests on 577 patients with 0.05–0.5% cinnamyl alcohol in base cream or 99% ethanol, applied for 24–48 h, and reported erythema in 11 patients and slight erythema in 10 additional patients.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Concentrations 0.5% to 5% in a base cream or ethyl alcohol; patches applied to back, forearm, upper arm for 24-48 h
evidence.support_text: Cyclopentadecanone was tested in a human patch test at concentrations ranging from 0.5% to 5% in a base cream or ethyl alcohol. No reactions were observed out of 60 patients (Takenaka et al., 1986).

evidence.experimental_conditions: cross-reactivity patch test; concentration not specified
evidence.support_text: Mathias, Caldwell, and Maibach (1979) reported a case of a laboratory technician with allergic contact dermatitis associated with the use of 80% hydroxyethylmethacrylate in absolute alcohol; the patient exhibited cross-reactivity to ethyl methacrylate (as well as methyl, propyl, and isopropyl methacrylate) by patch test, but not to butyl or isobutyl methacrylate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Dilutions of 10% and 20% AMP 100 in distilled water and ethyl alcohol; tested on 2 patients with airborne contact dermatitis and 8 asymptomatic subjects.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with AMP 100 at dilutions of 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 5%, 10%, and 20% in distilled water and ethyl alcohol was performed on 2 patients and 8 asymptomatic subjects. The patch tests proved positive (+/++) in the 10% and 20% dilutions of both vehicles in all subjects.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dose and vehicle not reported
evidence.support_text: In a series of patch tests from 1981-1986 in patients with contact dermatitis, one reaction to cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported) was observed (De Groot, 1987).

evidence.experimental_conditions: European standard series; 125 children under 12 years; patch tests read at 48 and 96 h according to ICDRG criteria; dose and vehicle for cinnamyl alcohol not reported (Rademaker and Forsyth, 1989).
evidence.support_text: In a study of 125 children under 12 years patch tested with the European standard series for contact dermatitis from 1981–1987, one patient reacted to cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported) with reactions read at 48 and 96 h according to ICDRG criteria.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human repeated insult patch test; dose administered to skin
evidence.support_text: Benzyl alcohol as a high DSA₀₅ of 48.67 µg/cm² (45.06 mol/m²) and a NOEL of 5,906 µg/cm² (5.47 mol/m²).

evidence.experimental_conditions: human skin sensitization test; no vehicle or concentration specified

evidence.experimental_conditions: human skin sensitization test; no vehicle or concentration specified

evidence.experimental_conditions: ICDRG standard series with fragrance mix and its components; 35 miners, 55 male and 30 female non-miners with eczematous skin problems; patch tests performed when eczema was quiescent; reactions read at 48 and 96 h; dose and vehicle for cinnamyl alcohol not reported (Goodfield and Saihan, 1988).
evidence.support_text: In a study of coal miners and non-miners with eczematous skin problems, 2 male non-miners showed positive patch test reactions to cinnamyl alcohol (dose and vehicle not reported) when tested with the ICDRG standard series including fragrance mix and its components; reactions were read at 48 and 96 h.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Initial test: 10%, 1%, 0.1% in ethanol, readings at D2 and D3. Second test: 5%, 1%, 0.1% in petrolatum, only 5% gave reaction (+ at D2 and D3). Control subjects (n=10) were negative except one with weak erythema (hyperirritable skin).
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch tested with the ingredients of the emollient cream and reacted weakly to resveratrol at concentrations of 10%, 1%, and 0.1% in ethanol (erythema with sharp edges at D2 and D3). In a subsequent test with resveratrol in petrolatum, the patient reacted to 5% only (+ at D2 and D3), while control subjects were negative except one with hyperirritable skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: not specified for this individual case; general method: occlusive patch test, 2 days occlusion, readings at day 2 and day 3/4, vehicle not specified
evidence.support_text: The paper describes clinical symptoms and a positive patch-test reaction to cetyl alcohol in a 15-month-old atopic baby, due to its presence in a pharmaceutical cream, indicating that cetyl alcohol caused allergic contact dermatitis in this patient.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 45-year-old female patient with face dermatitis from Avène® 20B 7A cream containing Euxyl K 400.
evidence.support_text: The patch test to phenoxy-ethanol was negative in the 45-year-old female patient allergic to Euxyl K 400.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with 10% cleansing tissue extract in alcohol on 5 healthy subjects.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with 10% concentration of the extract in alcohol on 5 healthy subjects: in the 2 subjects who experienced contact urticaria with the tissue itself, the extract caused an itchy reaction with erythema after several hours.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with calcipotriol 2 or 10 µg/ml in isopropyl alcohol, according to ESCD guidelines; patients with pre-existing dermatitis.
evidence.support_text: Allergic contact dermatitis was confirmed by patch testing in all 6 patients presenting with eczematous lesions complicating pre-existing dermatitis. Patch tests were performed with calcipotriol (2 or 10 µg/ml in isopropyl alcohol) according to ESCD guidelines, and the lesions improved following treatment with topical corticosteroids and/or oral medication.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with Finn Chambers, readings at 2, 4, and 7 days; interpretation per ICDRG guidelines. Hydrocortisone-17-butyrate was tested at 1% in ethanol.
evidence.support_text: One child (female, 6-year-old, SCORAD = 38.3) was patch-test positive to hydrocortisone-17-butyrate (tested at 1% in ethanol) among 71 children with atopic dermatitis. Readings were performed at 2, 4, and 7 days using Finn Chambers and interpreted according to ICDRG guidelines.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with Finn Chambers; readings at 2, 4, 7 days; ICDRG criteria; hydrocortisone-17-butyrate 1% in ethanol
evidence.support_text: The same child (1.4%) with atopic dermatitis (SCORAD=38.3) also showed a positive patch test reaction to hydrocortisone-17-butyrate (1% ethanol) at days 2, 4, and 7, indicating skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with fragrance mix and fragrance materials; 3% cinnamyl alcohol; 48 h contact; reading time not specified.
evidence.support_text: Ohela and Saramies (1983) reported that patch tests with 3% cinnamyl alcohol in 520 patients resulted in 5 positive reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with isopropyl myristate 10% alcohol; patient was a 64-year-old woman with eczematous rash from a commercial sunscreen
evidence.support_text: Bharati and King reported a 64-year-old woman who presented with an eczematous rash from a commercial sunscreen. A further patch test of the ingredients in the sunscreen resulted in positive reactions for isohexadacane 10% alcohol and isopropyl myristate 10% alcohol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tested with 1% ethanol using Finn Chambers, readings at 2, 4, and 7 days, interpreted according to ICDRG guidelines.
evidence.support_text: A 6-year-old female child with atopic dermatitis (SCORAD 38.3) showed a positive patch test reaction to hydrocortisone-17-butyrate (1% ethanol) using Finn Chambers with readings at 2, 4, and 7 days interpreted according to ICDRG guidelines.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch tests using A1-Test strips and Scanpor on upper back for 48 h; reactions read at patch removal and 24 h after; 5% cinnamyl alcohol in yellow soft paraffin.
evidence.support_text: Addo et al. (1982) tested 5% cinnamyl alcohol in yellow soft paraffin via 48 h patch tests on upper back in 50 patients with PD/AR, 32 with PLE, and 457 with contact dermatitis, reporting sensitization reactions in 2, 1, and 8 patients, respectively.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocyte cultures from SMX-NO-sensitized rats; treated with anti-MHC class I and/or anti-MHC class II antibodies; stimulated with soluble SMX-NO or SMX-NO-modified cells
evidence.support_text: Antibody blocking experiments showed that splenocyte cultures from rats administered SMX-NO, treated with anti-MHC class I or class II antibodies, did not proliferate or proliferated less in the presence of soluble SMX-NO compared to without antibodies (paragraph 32). Pretreatment of naive splenocytes with anti-MHC antibodies before SMX-NO addition (blocking direct MHC modification) only minimally decreased proliferation, indicating that antigen processing is required (paragraph 33).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from rats sensitized with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (1 mg/kg) restimulated ex vivo with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (10 µl/ml) for 72 h; cytokine measured in culture supernatant by ELISA.
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats restimulated with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (10 µl/ml) showed IFN-γ secretion (50, 16, 4, 153 pg/ml in four rats) while IL-4 was not significantly increased (1-10 pg/ml vs DMSO 4-12 pg/ml).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from rats sensitized with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (1 mg/kg) restimulated ex vivo with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (10 µl/ml) for 72 h; cytokine measured in culture supernatant by ELISA.
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats restimulated with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (10 µl/ml) showed IL-4 concentrations of 1, 6, 7, 10 pg/ml in four rats, not exceeding DMSO control values (4-12 pg/ml).

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo; male Wistar rats; dosing with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole; splenocytes re-stimulated ex vivo with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole.
evidence.support_text: Administration of nitroso sulphonamethoxazole to male Wistar rats resulted in a strong proliferative response of splenocytes on re-stimulation with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole; CD4+ or CD8+ depleted cells responded equally; the response was not inhibited by glutathione and cells produced IFN-γ, but not IL-4.

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo; male Wistar rats; dosing with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine; splenocytes re-stimulated ex vivo with test compounds.
evidence.support_text: Rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine did not respond to any of the test compounds, including the ex vivo splenocyte proliferation assay.

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo; male Wistar rats; dosing with sulphonamethoxazole; splenocytes re-stimulated ex vivo with test compounds (sulphonamethoxazole, hydroxylamine, nitroso).
evidence.support_text: Rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole did not respond to any of the test compounds, including the ex vivo splenocyte proliferation assay.

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo; male Wistar rats; pre-treated with diethyl maleate to deplete glutathione, then dosed with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine; splenocytes re-stimulated ex vivo with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole.
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from glutathione-depleted rats treated with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine responded weakly to nitroso sulphonamethoxazole, but not to sulphonamethoxazole or its hydroxylamine, upon ex vivo re-stimulation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: In vivo; male Wistar rats; primed with complete Freund's adjuvant, then dosed with sulphonamethoxazole; splenocytes re-stimulated ex vivo with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole.
evidence.support_text: Dosing of rats with sulphonamethoxazole produced a cellular response to nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (but not to sulphonamethoxazole or its hydroxylamine) when the animals were primed with complete Freund's adjuvant.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rats administered nitroso-SMX; splenocytes re-stimulated ex vivo with nitroso-SMX.
evidence.support_text: Rats administered nitroso-SMX exhibited a proliferative response of splenocytes upon ex vivo re-stimulation with nitroso-SMX.

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo T-cell restimulation proliferation assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole (after diethyl maleate pretreatment) were restimulated with test compounds
evidence.support_text: Splenocyte cultures from sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats (after diethyl maleate pretreatment) did not proliferate on restimulation with sulphonamethoxazole or sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine (P>0.05).

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo T-cell restimulation proliferation assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole (naïve) were restimulated with test compounds
evidence.support_text: Animals administered sulphonamethoxazole did not respond to any of the test compounds (P>0.05), indicating no T-cell proliferation.

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo T-cell restimulation proliferation assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine (doses not specified) were restimulated with various test compounds
evidence.support_text: Animals administered sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine did not respond to any of the test compounds (P>0.05), indicating no T-cell proliferation.

evidence.assay_type: ex vivo T-cell restimulation proliferation assay
evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine after diethyl maleate pretreatment were restimulated with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (10 µg ml⁻¹)

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs treated with SMX-NO; splenocytes isolated and stimulated ex vivo with SMX-NO. Combined AA and GSH deficiency did not enhance proliferation compared to replete controls.
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes isolated from guinea pigs treated with SMX-NO proliferated in response to ex-vivo SMX-NO stimulation. Combined ascorbate and glutathione deficiency did not lead to enhanced T cell proliferation compared to replete controls.

evidence.experimental_conditions: rat splenocytes
evidence.support_text: Incubation of SMX-NO with rat splenocytes led to remarkable toxicity and major histocompatibility complex-restricted antigen presentation (Naisbitt et al., 2001).

evidence.experimental_conditions: T cells from BALB/c mice primed with nitrosobenzene (two sc injections) were cocultured with aniline-pulsed WBMCs (1 mM aniline) in the presence of irradiated spleen APCs; proliferation measured.
evidence.support_text: Nitrosobenzene-primed T cells showed a recall response in vitro when cocultured with aniline-pulsed WBMCs and additional APCs, indicating that aniline-modified antigens are recognized by T cells induced by nitrosobenzene. This was observed in 4 out of 6 experiments, while T cells from solvent-primed mice never responded.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes isolated from SMX-NO-treated guinea pigs; in vitro restimulation with SMX-NO.
evidence.support_text: Cells isolated from the spleen of SMX-NO-treated guinea pigs exhibited SMX-NO-specific T cell proliferation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse spleen cells from BSA-colophony immunized mice, cells pooled from 3 mice per group, challenged with 50 µg/ml BSA-colophony antigen, experiment 1 only.
evidence.support_text: Spleen cells from mice primed with BSA-colophony conjugate showed a significantly greater mitogenic index to BSA-colophony challenge compared to other challenge antigens in experiment 1 (p ≤ 0.02), although the response was described as poor.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse spleen cells from HIG-colophony immunized mice, cells pooled from 3 mice per group, challenged with 50 µg/ml HIG-colophony antigen, mitogenic index calculated as log(cpm in presence of antigen) minus log(cpm in absence of antigen).
evidence.support_text: In experiment 1, HIG-colophony primed mouse spleen cells challenged with 50 µg/ml HIG-colophony conjugate showed a mitogenic index of 11.01 (cells pooled from three mice).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse spleen cells from HIG-colophony immunized mice, cells pooled from 3 mice per group, challenged with 50 µg/ml HIG-colophony antigen, mitogenic index calculated as log(cpm in presence of antigen) minus log(cpm in absence of antigen).
evidence.support_text: In experiment 2, HIG-colophony primed mouse spleen cells challenged with 50 µg/ml HIG-colophony conjugate showed a mitogenic index of 6.03 (cells pooled from three mice).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse splenocytes from BSA-colophony immunized mice stimulated with BSA-colophony conjugate; experiment 1.
evidence.support_text: In experiment 1, spleen cells from mice immunized with BSA-colophony showed a mitogenic index of 1.78 (SE 0.03) when stimulated with BSA-colophony, which was significantly different (p ≤ 0.02) from responses to BSA, HIG, or HIG-colophony.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse splenocytes from HIG-colophony immunized mice stimulated with HIG-colophony conjugate; experiment 1.
evidence.support_text: In experiment 1, spleen cells from mice immunized with HIG-colophony showed a mitogenic index of 11.01 (SE 0.64) when stimulated with HIG-colophony, which was significantly different (p ≤ 0.02) from responses to BSA-colophony, BSA, or HIG.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mouse splenocytes from HIG-colophony immunized mice stimulated with HIG-colophony conjugate; experiment 2.
evidence.support_text: In experiment 2, spleen cells from mice immunized with HIG-colophony showed a mitogenic index of 6.03 (SE 0.28) when stimulated with HIG-colophony, which was significantly different (p ≤ 0.02) from responses to other antigens.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Ex vivo, splenocytes from sulfamethoxazole- or sulfamethoxazole/S9-initiated mice, restimulation with drug and S9 bioactivating system
evidence.support_text: Splenocyte proliferation could be induced from sulfamethoxazole- or sulfamethoxazole/S9-initiated mice, but only with drug and the bioactivating system during restimulation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; oral mucosa-sensitized with NiSO4; splenocytes harvested after challenge; restimulated in vitro
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from skin-sensitized mice proliferated similarly to those from oral mucosa-sensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; orally-tolerized with NiSO4; splenocytes harvested after challenge; restimulated in vitro

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; skin-sensitized with NiSO4; splenocytes harvested after challenge; restimulated in vitro
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from skin-sensitized mice proliferated similarly to those from oral mucosa-sensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs on ascorbic acid (AA)-restricted diet, treated with buthionine sulfoximine (BSO) 250 mg/kg SC daily, and SMX-NO 1 mg/kg IP 4 days per week for 2 weeks; splenocytes stimulated ex vivo with SMX-NO.
evidence.support_text: Splenocyte proliferation in response to SMX-NO was not significantly increased in guinea pigs with combined AA and GSH deficiency treated with SMX-NO (1 mg/kg IP 4 days/week for 2 weeks).

evidence.experimental_conditions: rat splenocytes, antigen presented by MHC from cells haptenated with SMX-NO
evidence.support_text: Sensitized rat splenocytes proliferated in the presence of MHC-restricted antigen derived from cells haptenated with SMX-NO, for both viable and dead cells at low and high hapten levels.

evidence.experimental_conditions: species: pig (Sus scrofa); in vitro splenocyte proliferation assay; stimulation with SMX
evidence.support_text: In no pigs was the splenocyte response to SMX in vitro increased above vehicle control (SI 1.0 ± 0.34).

evidence.experimental_conditions: species: pig (Sus scrofa); in vitro splenocyte proliferation assay; stimulation with SMX-NO; groups: antioxidant-deficient and antioxidant-replete
evidence.support_text: No significant differences in SMX-NO-specific splenocyte proliferation were observed between deficient (SI, 3.6 ± 2.4) and replete (SI, 3.2 ± 2.8; P = 0.12) pigs treated with SMX-NO. evidence.experimental_conditions: splenocytes from adjuvant-primed rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole, restimulated with sulphonamethoxazole in vitro
evidence.support_text: Cells from all rats responded weakly to sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine, but not to sulphonamethoxazole.

evidence.experimental_conditions: splenocytes from all rats (including adjuvant-primed and nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated), restimulated with sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine in vitro
evidence.support_text: Cells from all rats responded weakly to sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine, but not to sulphonamethoxazole.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from NiSO₄-sensitized mice (skin or oral route) cultured for 72 hr, then pulsed with ³H-thymidine (0.2 µCi) for 16 hr, uptake measured by liquid scintillation counter.
evidence.support_text: Proliferation activity of splenocytes from NiSO₄-sensitized mice (both skin and oral routes) was significantly higher than that from untreated mice (p<0.05 for skin sensitized, p<0.001 for oral sensitized), as measured by ³H-thymidine uptake.

evidence.experimental_conditions: splenocytes from nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats (dose not specified in this paragraph), restimulated with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole in vitro; study referenced Table 2
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats proliferated in response to nitroso sulphonamethoxazole (Table 2). Adjuvant-primed rats dosed with sulphonamethoxazole did produce a response, but only to nitroso sulphonamethoxazole.

evidence.experimental_conditions: splenocytes from nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats; pulsing with 10 µg/ml nitroso sulphonamethoxazole; addition of 300 µg/ml glutathione; 0.1–72 h
evidence.support_text: Pulsing cultures with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole and the addition of glutathione, which reduces nitroso sulphonamethoxazole, did not prevent proliferation (Figure 7a, b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: splenocytes from nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-treated rats; restimulated with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole-modified serum protein (medium incubated with nitroso sulphonamethoxazole for 5 min, then glutathione added)

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from SMX-NO-treated rats (1 mg/kg) cultured with lysed or viable SMX-NO-modified naive irradiated antigen-presenting cells; proliferation measured by [3H]thymidine incorporation over 72 h incubation.

After 72 h, proliferation was determined by incorporation of [³H]thymidine over an additional 8 h. Results are presented as mean ± S.D. from four rats, with incubations carried out in triplicate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rats, in vivo injection of sulfamethoxazole plus adjuvant, ex vivo restimulation with SMX-NO

evidence.assay_type: splenocyte proliferation assay with CD4+/CD8+ depletion

evidence.support_text: No proliferation was observed with sulphonamethoxazole or sulphonamethoxazole hydroxylamine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from SMX-NO-sensitized rats (i.p. administration); in vitro restimulation with soluble SMX-NO (5-50 µM)
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from rats administered SMX-NO in vivo displayed a concentration-dependent proliferative response on in vitro restimulation with soluble SMX-NO at 5-50 µM. Concentrations above 50 µM inhibited proliferation (paragraph 30).

evidence.assay_type: T cell proliferation assay with SMX-NO-modified stimulator cells
evidence.experimental_conditions: Splenocytes from SMX-NO-sensitized rats; stimulated with SMX-NO-modified (10-250 µM, 5-min pulse) irradiated naive splenocytes or purified antigen-presenting cells, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells
evidence.support_text: Splenocytes from SMX-NO-sensitized rats proliferated in the presence of SMX-NO-modified (10-250 µM), irradiated naive splenocytes. A 5-min pulse with SMX-NO was sufficient for hapten formation and T cell proliferation (paragraph 30). In another experiment, SMX-NO-modified purified antigen-presenting cells, CD4+ T cells, or CD8+ T cells all induced similar proliferative responses from sensitized splenocytes (paragraph 31).

evidence.experimental_conditions: rats sensitized with SMX in CFA; splenocytes restimulated with SMX-NO in vitro
evidence.support_text: T cells from rats administered SMX in complete Freund's adjuvant proliferated on restimulation in vitro with SMX-NO but not with the parent drug SMX.
